title: Will the 30-year Mortgage Rate hit __ in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, for any week ending on or before December 31, 2026, the U.S. 30-year Fixed-Rate Mortgage (interest rate %) is equal to or above the listed rate, according to the Freddie Mac weekly Primary Mortgage Market Survey. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

The resolution source for this market will be Freddie Mac — specifically, the 30-year Fixed Rate Mortgage rates published through the weekly Primary Mortgage Market Survey, which can be viewed at https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms.

This market will resolve as soon as the 30-year Fixed-Rate Mortgage is equal to or greater than the listed price, or once data for the final week ending on or before December 31, 2026 has been published. If no data for the final week ending on or before December 31, 2026 has been published by January 14, 2027, 11:59 PM, this market will resolve based on the available data at that time.

Note: All published weekly levels of the 30-year Fixed-Rate Mortgage will be treated as final. Revisions to previously published data will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent 30-year fixed mortgage rates have climbed to 6.66% as of July 30, 2026, up from a February low near 5.98%, reflecting elevated 10-year Treasury yields and sticky inflation that reached 4.2% in May. With the Federal Reserve holding the federal funds rate steady after 2025 cuts and signaling data dependence at its July meeting, mortgage rates—tied more closely to longer-term bond markets than short-term policy—have faced upward pressure from persistent CPI readings and geopolitical oil shocks. Forecasts from Fannie Mae and the MBA point to year-end levels near 6.4%, implying limited scope for sharp declines absent cooler inflation or renewed rate-cut expectations. Upcoming CPI releases, labor-market data, and any FOMC communications through year-end represent key catalysts that could shift the market-implied path for hitting specific rate thresholds. Trader positioning on Polymarket aggregates these macroeconomic signals with real capital at risk.
